Rapid Recall

Use these short patterns before completing the homework questions and IDLE tasks.

01

Record toolkit

Use named dictionary fields for one record and a list for the collection.

record = {"id": "M01", "active": True}
records = [record]
02

File toolkit

Use with open and choose r, w or a deliberately.

with open("data.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    lines = file.readlines()
03

Search toolkit

Return failure only after every record has been checked.

for record in records:
    if record["id"] == target:
        return record
return None
04

Persistence toolkit

Update program data, then rewrite or append the correct stored record.

record["active"] = False
save_records(records)

    PYTHON LAB REFERENCE
    Support & examples
    A compact reminder of the Unit 5 toolkits.
    Key concepts
    • Dictionaries represent named records.
    • File modes control how stored data changes.
    • Searches must check every relevant record.
    • Persistent changes must be written back to a file.
    Common errors
    • Wrong dictionary key
    • Wrong file mode
    • Early failed-search return
    • Forgetting the newline
    Misconceptions to avoid
    Changing a dictionary always changes the file
    A program-memory update is persistent only after the changed data is written back.
    EXAMPLE 01 · COMBINED
    Load and search
    records = load_records("data.txt")
result = find_by_id(records, target)
    Keep loading and searching in separate functions.
